narrative.overview:
The owner console is a company control room you can read in ten seconds. Every owner screen opens on a page title with one line of summary, then a row of metric tiles that answer "is it alive, what did it cost, what needs me", then the work itself, laid out by state. The room is light by default (dark is the owner's opt-in under Settings > 화면, applied as `:root[data-theme="dark"]` with a full mirrored token set), quiet at rest, and loud only where a state demands it.

The material is paper-flat: a light neutral ground, white panels, and 1px hairlines. Depth comes from tone (ground, panel, panel-2) and borders, not from shadow. The primary action is ink, not brand colour; the single indigo accent marks what is selected, focused, linked, or in progress. Five state colours (blue running, amber waiting, green done, red failed or blocked, violet review) do real jobs on chips, board column headers, meters, and chart series, and nowhere else.

The signature move is the status board: any collection with states (decisions, owner to-dos, tasks) reads as columns with a state chip and a count, switchable to a list, with the choice remembered per screen. Density is operational, not airy: 14px body, 12 to 16px gaps, and a main column that uses the full width of the screen.
keyCharacteristics: Numbers first: PageHead, then a MetricGrid of tiles on every owner screen (12 pages ship it).
Flat at rest: hairline borders and tonal layers; shadows only as state feedback or for floating layers.
Ink primary buttons; one indigo accent for selection, focus, links, and progress.
State colours are semantic only, each paired with a soft background of the same hue.
Status board as the signature view, with board/list switching.
Pretendard Variable throughout, tabular numerals everywhere numbers appear, mono only for reference IDs and code.

rules.name: The State Means Colour Rule
rules.body: Run, warn, ok, bad, and info appear only when they encode a state. Each solid hue pairs with its own `-bg` wash; never use a state hue for decoration or emphasis.

rules.name: The Ink, Not Indigo Rule
rules.body: Primary actions are Console Ink. Indigo is reserved for selection, focus, links, and progress, so a coloured element always means "this one" or "this far".

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change (counts, money, times, percentages) uses tabular numerals so columns and tiles do not jitter under live updates.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Pretendard for everything; mono only for identifiers and code, never for prose or headings.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow at rest. A shadow means hover, selection, liveness, or a layer above the page.

rules.name: The No Nested Box Rule
rules.body: A bordered box never sits inside another bordered box. Entries inside a box are separated by hairline rules, not boxed again.

dos: **Do** open every owner screen with PageHead, then a MetricGrid, then sections.
**Do** lay any collection that has states out as a Board with chip-and-count column headers, and offer the list view through the segmented switch.
**Do** use Console Ink for the primary action and reserve indigo for selection, focus, links, and progress.
**Do** pair every state hue with its own `-bg` wash and use it only for that state.
**Do** use tabular numerals for every changing number and mono only for reference IDs and code.
**Do** define both light and dark values for any new token; light is the default.
**Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: live pulses stop and transitions drop.
donts: **Don't** fill buttons with indigo; that is the legacy `button.primary` look the kit overrides.
**Don't** nest a bordered box inside another; separate entries with hairlines.
**Don't** add shadows to surfaces at rest.
**Don't** use state colours for decoration, category, or brand emphasis.
**Don't** introduce a second display face or set prose or headings in mono.
**Don't** fix widths to Korean string lengths; the UI will also ship in English.
